title: extraReducers
description: Learn how to use extraReducers to handle actions from other slices and async thunks.

data.text: **extraReducers** lets a slice respond to actions defined in other slices — including lifecycle actions from `createAsyncThunk`. This is the key mechanism for cross-slice communication in Redux Toolkit.

In classic Redux, reducers only respond to their own action types. But real apps need to react to actions from other features. For example, when a `fetchUser` thunk succeeds, the `todos` slice might want to load that user's todos. `extraReducers` makes this possible.

`createSlice` provides an `extraReducers` field that accepts a builder function. The builder has an `addCase` method for registering handlers for specific action types. It also supports `addMatcher` and `addDefaultCase` for advanced scenarios.

data.title: Basic extraReducers

data.text: The most common use case for `extraReducers` is handling actions from `createAsyncThunk`. Since thunks dispatch `pending`, `fulfilled`, and `rejected` actions automatically, other slices can react to those lifecycle events.

data.content: Handling fetchUsers thunk actions in another slice

data.text: When to Use extraReducers vs Regular Reducers

`addMatcher` lets you handle actions conditionally. It takes a predicate function and a reducer. This is useful for filtering multiple action types or responding to patterns rather than specific actions.

data.title: addMatcher

data.text: `addDefaultCase` is the catch-all for any action not matched by `addCase` or `addMatcher`. Use it sparingly — explicit `addCase` calls are usually preferred for clarity and debugging.

data.title: addDefaultCase

data.text: When using `extraReducers`, the slice's state shape remains exactly the same. You're simply adding more reaction paths to the same reducer function. The `initialState` and `reducers` define the core behavior, while `extraReducers` handles external influences.

terms.definition: Field on createSlice that handles actions from other slices, thunks, or external sources.
Registers a reducer for a specific action type, typically used for thunk lifecycle actions.
Registers a reducer for actions matching a predicate function, useful for pattern-based handling.
Registers a reducer for any unmatched action, acting as a fallback.

data.text: Instead of the builder function, you can pass `extraReducers` as an object with action type strings as keys. This is less common but still valid. The builder pattern is preferred for readability and TypeScript support.
